notes: Nill Download Manager 2.3.2 keeps long downloads alive and makes browser starts feel instant. A download whose link expires mid-transfer now heals itself: instead of slowing down and failing, it refreshes its address and resumes from the byte it had reached — for ordinary files and for browser-started video alike — while a paused download is never woken by a refresh, and a file that changed behind its link restarts cleanly from zero. Facebook's picker is now instant: the quality list comes from the page's own data the moment the card opens — on posts, watch pages and the feed — each video on a busy page is offered on its own, and a video the page cannot identify is reported plainly instead of quietly downloading the wrong file. Downloads started from the browser begin sooner, with the click-to-start path roughly three times quicker than before, and the browser's own user agent now travels with browser-started downloads instead of a fixed one. The end of a download is tighter too: the tail of a file no longer waits on its slowest connection, a finished side of a video and audio pair lends its connections to the side still running, and a video whose audio is already in the right format is no longer re-encoded after the last byte, removing a long pause before the finish. On Linux the package now declares everything its icons need, and the progress dialog's Cancel button closes it once a download has finished.
